correctness.rationale: The original Algorithm 1 is algebraically reduced to its exact full two-state matrix. Three exact Jury expressions yield necessary and sufficient global stability; positivity of first from F>P, strict inequalities for the other two, and boundary eigenvalues establish the complete window. Symbolic factorization proves the Jordan collision u_c(v); AM-GM yields 17. Endpoint monotonicity gives the exact common-relaxation cutoff. The nonlinear witness has exact weak-concavity modulus 5/8, objective curvature >=5, beta=1<=8/5, Jacobian M(20,5,tau), and its spectral radius >1 for all tau. Verification from the included code checked these identities and 1200 independent sample cases, with the universal conclusions proved analytically.

value.rationale: Separates existence of an individually stable relaxation from robustness of one relaxation across a continuum of weakly concave curvatures; the exact universal thresholds 17 and (5+sqrt57)/2 are structural tuning boundaries, not arbitrary isolated numerics. The smooth strongly convex witness with positive and admissibly bounded weak-concavity parameter shows objective strong convexity and beta weak-concavity safety are insufficient for relaxation-only local stability at large alpha. These provide a motivated restriction to consider when applying four-operator splitting, beyond routine restatement of published sufficient convergence bounds.
